title: Third Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19
what_it_is: Third Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19

sections.label: Vaccine safety and efficacy approval
sections.summary: The Committee concluded the vaccine meets WHO, international and HSA safety and efficacy requirements, and the Government accepted these recommendations in full.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Committee has concluded that the vaccine meets the safety and efficacy requirements of the World Health Organization and other international regulatory authorities as well as that of our own HSA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted these recommendations in full.

sections.label: Vaccine quantity and supply assurance
sections.summary: Specific order quantities cannot be disclosed due to commercial sensitivities, but enough vaccines are secured for all Singaporeans and long-term residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I am not at liberty to disclose the specific quantity ordered due to commercial sensitivities and confidentiality undertakings in our advance purchase agreements with the vaccine manufacturers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: However, I can assure Members that we have secured enough vaccines for all Singaporeans and long-term residents in Singapore.

sections.label: Vaccine supply timeline
sections.summary: If all goes according to schedule, there will be enough vaccines for everyone by the third quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: If all goes according to schedule, we will have enough vaccines for everyone by the third quarter this year.

sections.label: Vaccination priority groups and schedule
sections.summary: COVID-19 frontline and essential personnel will be prioritised, with elderly and higher-risk groups starting February 2021, beginning with seniors aged 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will also prioritise COVID-19 frontline and other essential personnel, including swabbers hired by the Health Promotion Board, staff working at Government Quarantine Facilities, Community Care Facilities and dedicated Stay-Home Notice Facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We plan to start vaccinating our elderly and those at greater risk of severe disease from COVID-19 infection starting from February 2021, beginning with seniors aged 70 and above.

sections.label: 1959 smallpox vaccination campaign
sections.summary: The last vaccination of this scale was in 1959, in response to a smallpox outbreak where slightly over one million people were vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The last time we did a vaccination of this scale was in 1959, in response to an outbreak of smallpox where slightly over one million people were vaccinated.

sections.label: Vaccination uptake and two doses
sections.summary: Everyone is encouraged to come forward when their turn comes, noting some vaccines like Pfizer-BioNTech require two doses 21 days apart and up to 14 more days for maximum protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We encourage everyone to come forward for your vaccination when your turn comes so that we can increase our coverage as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We should also bear in mind that some vaccines, such as the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, will require two doses, 21 days apart, and it will take up to another 14 days after the second dose to achieve maximum protection against the virus.

sections.label: HSA PSAR vaccine assessment
sections.summary: Under the Pandemic Special Access Route, HSA experts apply strict international standards to assess COVID-19 vaccines for quality, safety and efficacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Under HSA's Pandemic Special Access Route (PSAR), HSA's scientific and clinical experts apply strict international standards to assess COVID-19 vaccines to ensure that they meet the stipulated high standards of quality, safety and efficacy.

sections.label: Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine authorised
sections.summary: HSA reviewed the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine through this process and authorised its use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: HSA has put the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine through this rigorous review process and has authorised its use.

sections.label: Expert Committee vaccine assessment
sections.summary: The Expert Committee assessed the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine as 95% efficacious in reducing symptomatic COVID-19 in persons aged 16 and older, with a safety profile consistent with other registered vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Expert Committee has assessed that the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine demonstrated a high vaccine efficacy of 95% in reducing symptomatic COVID-19 disease among persons aged 16 and older and its safety profile is consistent with that of other established and registered vaccines used in immunisation against other diseases.

sections.label: Allergy advice and financial assistance
sections.summary: HSA and the Expert Committee recommended that those with known severe allergies not be vaccinated, recipients be observed 30 minutes post-vaccination, and MOH introduce a vaccine injury financial assistance programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: HSA and the Expert Committee have therefore recommended that those with known severe allergies should not be vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: All vaccine recipients should also be observed on-site for 30 minutes post-vaccination, so that any severe allergic reactions such as anaphylaxis can be detected and treated promptly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MOH will also introduce a vaccine injury financial assistance programme to provide support for persons who suffer a serious adverse event that is assessed to be related to COVID-19 vaccines administered in Singapore.

sections.label: Free COVID-19 vaccination access
sections.summary: COVID-19 vaccination will be free for all Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and long-term residents, totalling about 5.7 million people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To ensure access to the vaccine, COVID-19 vaccination will be free for all Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and long-term residents in Singapore, which includes Employment Pass, S Pass, and Work Permit holders, Foreign Domestic Workers, and Dependent Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass and Student Pass holders – totalling about 5.7 million people.

sections.label: Physical vaccination card
sections.summary: Every vaccinated person will receive a physical vaccination card reminding them of their second dose appointment, showing which vaccine was administered, and giving post-vaccination advice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Every person who is vaccinated will receive a physical vaccination card and this will help remind them of their appointment to return for their second dose, indicate clearly which vaccine was administered and provide brief post-vaccination advice.

sections.label: Vaccine allocation criteria
sections.summary: Vaccine allocation will be based largely on medical indications, suitability for population groups, and vaccine availability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The allocation of vaccines will largely be based on medical indications of the different vaccines and the suitability of the vaccine for the different population groups, as well as availability of the vaccines.

sections.label: Survey on vaccination willingness
sections.summary: Findings showed close to 60% would get vaccinated if a vaccine becomes available in Singapore, while about a third preferred to wait for more data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our findings showed that more than half – close to 60% – say they would get vaccinated if a vaccine becomes available in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: About a third were more cautious, saying they would prefer to wait for more data before deciding.

sections.label: Claims about Pfizer-BioNTech trial deaths
sections.summary: Claims said six people died due to the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine in clinical trials, but only two of the six received the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, there were claims that six people had died due to the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine during clinical trials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: However, the facts are that only two of the six individuals were given the vaccine and the other four were given the placebo.

sections.label: Vaccines secured for whole population
sections.summary: Vaccinations will be a key enabler for returning to normalcy, and enough vaccines have been secured for the whole population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Vaccinations will be a key enabler for us to return to normalcy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have secured enough vaccines for the whole population.

sections.label: Rallying together and Phase Three
sections.summary: Rallying and working together, adapting, and regaining footing after setbacks brought things under control and enabled Phase Three on 28 December last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: What matters most at the end of the day is our ability to rally and work together, to adapt along the way and to regain our footing after setbacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is how we were able to bring things under control, keep community transmission low, and move to Phase Three on 28 December last year.

sections.label: UK and South Africa travel measures
sections.summary: From the UK and South Africa, additional testing and requirements were introduced, and the number of travellers was restricted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, from the UK and South Africa we have introduced additional testing and requirements, as well as restricted the number of travellers.

sections.label: Marine workers testing sweep
sections.summary: A one-time sweep tests all marine workers, and testing frequency is increased for marine workers going on board vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Likewise, we are doing a one-time sweep to test all marine workers and we are increasing the frequency of testing for marine workers going on board vessels.

sections.label: Travellers from China
sections.summary: Around 500 travellers have arrived from China under this arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Around 500 travellers have arrived from China under this arrangement.

sections.label: Connect@Singapore travel lane
sections.summary: A new travel lane, Connect@Singapore, is aimed at a limited number of business, officials and high economic value travellers for short-term stays.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Recently, we also announced a new travel lane, called Connect@Singapore, aimed at a limited number of business, officials and high economic value travellers coming to Singapore for short-term stays.

sections.label: Travellers without pre-departure tests
sections.summary: Between 18 November and 27 December, over 12,000 travellers from higher risk countries entered without pre-departure tests; around 100 tested positive and none caused local transmission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But through the SHN, we ensure that community transmission risks are minimised for these travellers, even in the absence of a pre-departure test.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, in response to Mr Gerald Giam’s query, between 18 November and 27 December last year, there have been over 12,000 travellers, including citizens and PRs, from higher risk countries and regions who entered Singapore without pre-departure tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So far around 100 or 0.85% have tested positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Importantly, none of these cases has resulted in local transmission.

sections.label: Hotel staff testing regime
sections.summary: All hotel staff in contact with SHN individuals will be placed on a 14-day rostered routine testing regime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As an additional safeguard, all hotel staff in contact with SHN individuals will henceforth be placed on a 14-day rostered routing testing regime or RRT.

sections.label: Possible SHN relaxation for vaccinated
sections.summary: If clear evidence shows transmission risks can be lowered significantly, relaxation to the SHN regime for vaccinated travellers will be considered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To Ms He Ting Ru’s question, if there is clear evidence that transmission risks can be lowered significantly, then we will certainly consider some relaxation to the SHN regime for vaccinated travellers.

sections.label: Weekly COVID-19 surveillance testing numbers
sections.summary: In December last year, more than 14,000 individuals were tested weekly on average through this surveillance mechanism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On average, we have tested more than 14,000 individuals every week in December last year, through this surveillance mechanism.

sections.label: Rapid test kit costs
sections.summary: The first rapid test kits in Singapore cost about $80 per person, but can now be done for under $50.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The first of such rapid test kits administered in Singapore cost about $80 per person.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is not just the test itself, but also the operation and manpower costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Now, it is possible to do this for under $50 per person, and the cost is likely to come down further.

sections.label: Spending on TraceTogether and SafeEntry
sections.summary: Around $10 million has been spent developing the TraceTogether app and SafeEntry system, which stopped transmission and saved lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To date, we have spent around $10 million on developing both the TraceTogether app and SafeEntry system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Well, the results speak for themselves – TraceTogether has stopped the transmission of the virus in many instances and has helped save many lives.

sections.label: TraceTogether participation numbers
sections.summary: More than 4.2 million people, around 78% of Singapore residents, now participate in TraceTogether, with about two million using only the app.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: More than 4.2 million people or around 78% of Singapore residents now participate in the TraceTogether programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Quite a number, around two million or slightly less than half, just use the TraceTogether app on their phones.

sections.label: TraceTogether token distribution resumption
sections.summary: Token distribution across all CCs was not completed, but inventory is being built up to resume distribution before requiring TraceTogether at SafeEntry checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why, as mentioned by Mr Lim Biow Chuan, we were not able to complete the distribution of the tokens across all the CCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have been steadily building up the inventory of the TraceTogether tokens and will soon be able to resume distribution in the CCs that are currently closed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After everyone who needs a token has had a chance to collect one, we will put in place the requirement to use TraceTogether only at the SafeEntry checkpoints.

sections.label: Pandemic peak case numbers
sections.summary: At the peak of the pandemic, there were more than 1,000 cases per day and the healthcare system was at risk of being overwhelmed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the peak of the pandemic, we had more than 1,000 cases per day, and our healthcare system was at risk of being overwhelmed.

sections.label: Priority for healthcare workers
sections.summary: The key priority is to focus on healthcare workers because they are on the frontline dealing with patients who could be infected with COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the key priority today is to focus on healthcare workers because they are at the frontline and they are dealing with the patients and some of them could be, in fact, infected with COVID-19.

sections.label: Other categories including military police
sections.summary: Other categories being looked at include the military, Police force, foreign representatives and embassies overseas, particularly in countries with high COVID-19 prevalence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Beyond this, we are also looking at different categories of people including key entities like our military, our Police force, which are very important in ensuring law and order, and national security, as well as our foreign representatives, our embassies overseas, particularly in countries where there is a high prevalence of COVID-19.

sections.label: Expanding vaccination quickly
sections.summary: The key is to protect people by expanding vaccination as quickly as possible to cover as many people as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do want to protect them as much as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, the key really is to expand our vaccination as quickly as possible to cover as many people as possible.

sections.label: Israel vaccination percentage
sections.summary: As from today, Israel has already vaccinated 12% of their population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As from today, Israel has already vaccinated 12% of their population.

sections.label: Healthcare workers vaccination timeline
sections.summary: The hope is that healthcare workers should be vaccinated within the next two weeks and it should be completed as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In fact, I hope that the healthcare workers should be vaccinated within the next two weeks and it should be completed as soon as possible.

sections.label: Efficacy threshold of 50%
sections.summary: WHO, the US and Singapore all have a minimum efficacy threshold of 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, on the question of efficacy threshold, it is true that WHO and the US, have a threshold of 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We, too, have a minimum threshold of 50%.

sections.label: HSA interim approval vaccine
sections.summary: HSA gave interim approval for the vaccine because full authorisation requires long-term data, which will be monitored over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We need to do this continuously for a prolonged period of time – usually one year, two years or maybe longer – so as to give us assurance of the long-term effect of this vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is part of the reason why HSA has not given a full authorisation because a full authorisation will require these long-term data to be available before we do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But in view of the pandemic that we are facing today, HSA has given an interim approval for the use of this vaccine, accepting the fact that long-term data will only be available in the long term and we will need to continue to monitor and to make our assessment in the long term.

sections.label: Diversifying vaccine sources
sections.summary: More vaccines being approved gives alternatives, and diversifying sources ensures access to other supplies if one shipment is delayed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are also looking forward to more vaccines being approved so we have alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We want to make sure that we diversify our sources of vaccines so that even if one shipment is delayed, we have access to other supplies.

sections.label: Assessing vaccination transmission risk
sections.summary: The extent to which vaccinations can help reduce transmission risk is still being assessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have mentioned just now, we are still assessing the extent to which vaccinations can help reduce transmission risk.

sections.label: No changes until vaccine effects known
sections.summary: Until the effects of the vaccine are understood, no changes can be made to domestic or travel measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Yes, there will be some beneficial impact but what is the extent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, until we understand the effects of the vaccine, I think we will not be able to make any changes to our measures, be domestic or travel measures.

sections.label: Vaccinated may skip pre-event test
sections.summary: Potentially, someone who has been vaccinated might not need to take a pre-event test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Potentially, if you have been vaccinated, we might say: well, someone who has been vaccinated need not take such a pre-event test.

sections.label: Sufficient quantity and vaccine portfolio
sections.summary: A sufficient quantity has been secured for the whole population, with a portfolio of vaccines rather than a single supplier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I thought I have answered the question on quantity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I will not be able to give a specific number but suffice to say that we have secured a sufficient quantity for the whole population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our strategy is also to ensure that we have a portfolio of vaccines and not just rely on a single supplier.

sections.label: Singaporeans willing to be vaccinated
sections.summary: The Minister said recent surveys showed over 60% of Singaporeans were prepared to be vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to my question, the answer provided by the Minister earlier is that, based on the recent surveys, over 60% of Singaporeans were prepared to be vaccinated.

sections.label: Advice on unapproved vaccines
sections.summary: The advice is not to wait for Sinovac or other unapproved vaccines, as their availability and approval are unknown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: With regard to Sinovac or any other vaccine that has not been approved, my advice is, do not wait for them because we do not know when they will be available and we also do not know whether they will be approved at all.

sections.label: Focus on Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine
sections.summary: People should focus on the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine available today and get vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Focus on what we have today, that is the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine and get vaccinated.

sections.label: Free battery replacement for tokens
sections.summary: Batteries in current tokens need replacement, and an implementation process will facilitate this free for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In terms of battery replacement, yes, for the tokens that we have today, the batteries will need to be replaced and we will put in place an implementation process to facilitate that for free, for everyone.

sections.label: One-for-one token swap approach
sections.summary: A one-for-one swap may be easier in other instances, and all factors were considered, including the current model's need for swaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In other instances, it may be easier to do a one-for-one swap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we have indeed taken into consideration all of these factors including the fact that with the current model, you may need to do a one-for-one swap, but we overall still think that this approach, given the circumstances, given the urgency of rolling out the tokens, was a better approach.

sections.label: Pregnant women advised against vaccination
sections.summary: Pregnant women are advised not to be vaccinated for now because data is insufficient, with research continuing as data emerges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In my speech, I explained that specifically for pregnant women, because the data is insufficient for the time being, therefore, we have advised pregnant women not to be vaccinated for the time being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are continuing to do research to study the effects on pregnant women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As data emerges, we will look at the data and reassure ourselves whether it is safe for pregnant women to take the vaccination.

sections.label: Smartphone users and tokens
sections.summary: For those who have smartphones, there is no need to collect the token.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For those who have smartphones, there is really no need to collect the token.

sections.label: App features and token distribution
sections.summary: The app will be made more useful to encourage app use, but tokens will still be available to reduce anxieties over TraceTogether-only SafeEntry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will try to make the app more useful, add more features and hopefully, when we do that, it will further tilt the balance and encourage more people in favour of using the app as opposed to the tokens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But to the extent that Singaporeans want to collect the tokens, I think we do want to make them available, reduce any anxieties associated with the roll-out of to TraceTogether-only SafeEntry and that is why we are doing this one time distribution.

sections.label: Testing capacity and TraceTogether uptake
sections.summary: There is capacity to test more frequently using rapid tests, and 78% of people in Singapore are on TraceTogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have the capacity to test more frequently and we are going to do more, using rapid test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have 78% of people in Singapore on TraceTogether.

sections.label: Vaccination and opening up
sections.summary: Vaccination can allow more opening up, but a significant number vaccinated is expected only by the third quarter, so big relaxations should not be rushed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The one thing that can allow us to open up more is vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we will only be able to get people vaccinated, a significant number of people vaccinated, as we said, by the third quarter of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, between now and the third quarter of the year, let us not rush to make big changes and big relaxations.

sections.label: Vaccination for those below 16
sections.summary: Those below 16 are strongly discouraged from volunteering for vaccination because the initial clinical trial did not include them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On the first question, I would strongly discourage those below 16 to volunteer for vaccination, primarily because the initial clinical trial did not include those below 16.

sections.label: Vaccination benefits for activities
sections.summary: Potential changes and adjustments are being studied, and vaccination will likely allow benefits such as exemption from certain requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And we are studying what are the potential changes and adjustments that we might allow and consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, it is not going to be a situation where we say, "No, you can't do this." But it is more likely to be a situation where vaccination will allow you some benefits in terms of activities, in terms of being exempted from certain requirements.

sections.label: Pre-Departure PCR Test Exclusions
sections.summary: Minister addresses which travellers are excluded from Pre-Departure PCR testing and notes high-risk arrivals are quarantined regardless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify which categories of travellers are excluded from the Pre-Departure PCR Test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Did all the 12,000 travellers who entered Singapore without a Pre-Departure PCR Test, fall under these categories and, of the 100 imported cases who did not have a Pre-Departure PCR Test, were any of them supposed to have had the test but did not do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, this is not a cheeky question but I believe it will give Singaporeans more assurance to take the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And, lastly, is HSA evaluating the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine which was already approved by the UK on 30 December?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I have not looked at the data in great detail but, based on the information we have put out, that the 12,000 which I cited, would largely comprise of these visitors or these returnees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But as I have highlighted and emphasised, whether someone does a Pre-Departure Test or not, so long as they come into Singapore from a high-risk country, we subject them to a quarantine, SHN.

sections.label: No Significant Virus Shift
sections.summary: There has largely been no evidence of significant change in virus severity or vaccine effectiveness in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: By and large, up to today, there has not been evidence to show significant shift in the severity of the virus or the impact on the effectiveness of the current vaccines that are being approved or reviewed in Singapore.

sections.label: HSA Rolling Review Approach
sections.summary: HSA has adopted a progressive rolling review approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: HSA has now adopted a progressive rolling review approach.

sections.label: Islandwide Vaccination Centres and GPs
sections.summary: Vaccination centres will be set up islandwide and private GPs engaged, as the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine is challenging to handle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For the general public, we will set up vaccination centres across the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we would not be able to squeeze everyone into the polyclinics for vaccination and that is why we also will need vaccination centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will also be working with private General Practitioners (GPs) clinics to help us to administer the vaccine, especially for those who are less mobile and will need to get to a clinic that is nearby.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Having said that, we have to bear in mind that this particular vaccine – the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine – is quite challenging to handle.

sections.label: Mobile Teams for Nursing Homes
sections.summary: Mobile vaccination teams will be deployed to nursing homes and senior care centres for less mobile residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For nursing homes and senior care centres – yes, we will make special arrangements to make sure that we are able to vaccinate them because many of them are not mobile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are planning to set up mobile vaccination teams that will be deployed to some of these nursing homes and senior care centres to provide vaccination services for them.
